summary: Newcastle United were knocked out of the Champions League group stage after a 2-1 loss to AC Milan at St James' Park, having led through a Joelinton strike. Christian Pulisic equalised and substitute Samuel Chukwueze scored the winner, sending Milan to the Europa League and Newcastle out of Europe. The piece argues Newcastle played well enough to win but were undone by injuries, tired legs and Milan's goalkeeping and depth, also recalling Mbappe's late equaliser in Paris.
one_line: Newcastle lost 2-1 to AC Milan after leading through Joelinton, finishing bottom of the Champions League group of death and leaving Europe entirely.
key_facts: Newcastle United lost to AC Milan after leading, their second cruel comeback defeat in as many Champions League games.
For roughly 45 minutes, including half-time, Newcastle were second in the group table, imagining a knockout tie with Real Madrid or Bayern Munich.
Christian Pulisic equalised for Milan and Samuel Chukwueze scored the winner, meaning the Europa League place went to AC Milan.
Joelinton scored Newcastle's goal with a rising shot from the edge of the box past Mike Maignan, after taking Miguel Almiron's pass.
Pulisic's equaliser came around the time Warren Zaire-Emery drew Paris Saint-Germain level against Borussia Dortmund.
Milan's winner came from three substitutes: Luka Jovic found Noah Okafor, who picked out Chukwueze to beat Martin Dubravka.
Fabian Schar had charged into the Milan box, leaving Newcastle short at the back; Theo Hernandez almost scored from the halfway line and Fikayo Tomori hit the post.
Fikayo Tomori made a goal-line tackle to stop Miguel Almiron scoring from Joelinton's low cross at 0-0.
Maignan tipped Bruno Guimaraes' 20-yard shot onto the bar; Newcastle had 17 shots, eight on target, while Milan had two on target.
Injured goalkeeper Nick Pope was missed; he had denied Milan victory at San Siro with a string of saves.
Kieran Trippier and Anthony Gordon were taken off because they seemed exhausted, and Eddie Howe had only one attacking substitute, Alexander Isak.
Newcastle finished with one win and five points in their first Champions League campaign in two decades.
Pulisic had been a Newcastle target the previous January before joining Milan in the summer.
Kylian Mbappe scored a controversial 98th-minute leveller in Paris in the earlier game.
